title: Goal Kick Build-Up Strategies
definition: A tactical framework for restarting play from a goal kick that combines short passing sequences with long distribution to manipulate opponent pressing structures.
content: Modern goal kick restarts require teams to treat the goalkeeper as an active outfield player to navigate high-pressing systems. Relying solely on short passes makes teams predictable, while consistent long balls allow opponents to settle defensively. Effective strategies blend these approaches: using short sequences to manipulate pressing lines and create space, then exploiting gaps with longer switches or penetrative passes. The build-up zone has expanded, demanding that centre-backs operate as complete players capable of receiving under pressure and turning in both directions. Full-backs need strong first-touch control for advanced distributions, while midfielders must scan and use two-footed technique to escape pressure. Goalkeepers require three-dimensional vision to judge angles and distances for difficult passes. Teams should categorize their options into five types: supporting play to centre-backs, passing through press lines to midfielders, delivering to advanced wide areas, direct forward play to strikers, and passes behind defensive lines. By varying these methods, teams can exploit spacing dynamics; for instance, narrow centre-back positioning opens wing space, while wider positioning creates central opportunities. Goalkeepers must maintain positioning to recycle possession if initial passes return, ensuring seamless continuation of the attacking sequence.

source.name: FIFA Training Centre: Different strategies when building out from goal kicks
